questions.q: Which statement best describes the inheritance pattern of nuclear DNA compared to mitochondrial DNA?
options: Nuclear DNA is inherited solely from the mother, while mitochondrial DNA is inherited from both parents.
Both nuclear and mitochondrial DNA are inherited exclusively from the mother.
Nuclear DNA is inherited from both parents, whereas mitochondrial DNA is inherited maternally.
Nuclear DNA is inherited from the father only, and mitochondrial DNA is inherited from the mother only.
questions.explain: Nuclear DNA is a combination of genetic material from both the biological mother and father. Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is inherited exclusively from the mother. Source: Nuclear DNA vs. Mitochondrial DNA.

questions.q: A forensic anthropologist unearths severely degraded skeletal remains exposed to environmental elements for over 50 years. What type of DNA analysis is most likely to yield a successful profile?
options: Nuclear DNA analysis, because bone marrow preserves it perfectly.
Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) analysis, because there are hundreds of copies of mtDNA per cell.
Y-chromosome analysis, because it resists degradation better than autosomal DNA.
Messenger RNA (mRNA) analysis, because RNA is more chemically stable than DNA over time.
questions.explain: Mitochondrial DNA is highly abundant (hundreds to thousands of copies per cell) compared to the single set of nuclear DNA per cell. It is extremely useful for degraded remains or hair shafts. Source: Mitochondrial DNA (useful for degraded remains).

questions.q: A suspect drops a hair at a crime scene. Upon microscopic examination, the hair shaft is present, but the follicular tag (the root) is completely absent. Which type of DNA can be successfully recovered and analyzed from this evidence?
options: Only nuclear DNA
Only mitochondrial DNA
Both nuclear and mitochondrial DNA
Neither, as hair shafts do not contain any genetic material
questions.explain: The follicular tag contains cellular material rich in nuclear DNA. Without the root, the keratinized hair shaft primarily retains mitochondrial DNA, making mtDNA analysis the only viable option. Source: Mitochondrial DNA.

questions.q: In a sexual assault investigation, analysts often encounter mixtures of male and female DNA. What specific type of STR analysis is highly beneficial for isolating the male suspect's genetic profile in a mixture overwhelmed by female victim DNA?
options: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) analysis
Y-STR analysis
RFLP restriction mapping
Next Generation Sequencing of the X chromosome
questions.explain: Y-STR analysis targets Short Tandem Repeats on the male-specific Y-chromosome. Female DNA does not contain a Y-chromosome and will not amplify during a Y-STR test, isolating the male profile.

questions.q: Which statement regarding mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) in forensics is false?
options: It is found outside the nucleus in the cell's cytoplasm.
It is structured as a closed, circular loop of DNA.
It is inherited maternally, meaning all siblings sharing the same biological mother have identical mtDNA.
It provides a higher power of individual discrimination than analyzing the 20 nuclear STR core loci.
questions.explain: Because mtDNA is inherited unchanged from the mother, it is not strictly unique to an individual (maternal relatives share it). Therefore, its discriminatory power is lower than nuclear DNA STR profiling, which can uniquely identify one individual.
